title: Trail Cameras Show Coyotes Using the World’s Largest Wildlife Crossing - Nautilus
gist: Trail cameras recorded two coyotes using the unfinished $114 million Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing over L.A.'s 101 freeway in late October 2026, ahead of its December official opening.

insights.claim: The Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing over the 10-lane 101 freeway in California recorded its first animal users when a coyote crossed on October 28, 2026, followed days later by a second coyote, before the bridge's official December opening.
insights.so_what: Early-use evidence supports the case for public funding of wildlife-crossing infrastructure, a niche for civil-engineering and habitat-restoration contractors.
insights.quote: A coyote used it to cross the 101 freeway on October 28th
insights.locator: The new Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing
insights.speaker: David Nield

insights.claim: The Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing is a roughly 210-foot-long, 174-foot-wide bridge in a $114 million project that also includes a second wildlife bridge and 13 acres of restored habitat, linking the Simi Hills to the Santa Monica Mountains.
insights.so_what: Benchmarks cost and scale (~$114M) for future urban wildlife-crossing projects.
insights.quote: The $114 million project will also include a second wildlife bridge and 13 acres of restored habitat.
insights.speaker: David Nield
